newsitem.title: USA: U.S. researcher says spanking worsens misbehavior.
newsitem.headline: U.S. researcher says spanking worsens misbehavior.

text.p: Regularly spanking a child for misbehaving causes distrust for the parent and provokes worse behavior in the long term, a U.S. researcher said Thursday.

Based on interviews with the mothers of roughly 3,000 children, University of New Hampshire sociologist Murray Straus said corporal punishment proved to be counterproductive, resulting in the child doing more lying, bullying, breaking things and other antisocial behavior.

"Spanking chips away at the child's liking for and trust of the parent. They're less likely to take the parents' values, and more likely to take influences from other kids which you might not want," Straus told Reuters. "One has to look at long-term effects of these things."

The interviews with the mothers of children in three age groups were done two years apart. The mothers were asked about the frequency of spanking and whether the child cheated or told lies, bullied or was cruel to others, felt remorse for misbehavior, broke things deliberately, was disobedient in school, or had trouble with teachers.
Of 807 mothers of 6- to 9-year-olds, 44 percent reported spanking their children in the previous week, and they meted out the punishment more than twice that week.
"We wanted to know: When parents spank, does behavior change for the worse, for the better or is there no difference? What we found was that it changes behavior for the worse," Straus said.
His report appeared in the medical journal Archives of Pediatrics & Adolescent Medicine.
Previous research has shown that 90 percent of U.S. parents spank their children, and a majority of pediatricians and psychologists do not discourage occasional corporal punishment, Straus said.

"But the best kept secret of child psychology is people turning away from corporal punishment," he said. Signs warning against spanking can be spotted in pediatricians' offices and more parents are learning to avoid the practice.
Spanking has been linked to low self-esteem, depression and low educational attainment, it said.
